bugs: config/queue.php:76-84: redis-long uses env('REDIS_QUEUE','default'), the same Redis list as the 'redis' connection. With QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis, a plain `queue:work` pops SyncSupplierStock from queues:default with retry_after=90, so after 90s the 20-40 minute run is released to another worker. With Tries(1) it is then failed, which also releases the unique lock. The file's own comment (SyncSupplierStock.php:14-15) warns about exactly this, so the no-double-run guarantee depends on how workers are deployed
tests/Feature/SyncSupplierStockTest.php:21-27 is named 'dispatched only once while a previous run holds the unique lock' but dispatches only once, so it does not test uniqueness at all

tests/Feature/SyncSupplierStockTest.php:12-19 'runs handle() repeatedly' asserts uniqueId only, so it is a near-empty test
ScheduleTest.php:51-58 runs schedule:run once, so it does not show that several servers running the scheduler produce a single dispatch
strengths: chunkById with a delete that re-applies the abandonedFor scope is memory-safe and race-safe (passes the 2500-row test)

v.rationale: I rank impl-1 first. Both implementations pass their tests (impl-1 24/24, impl-2 15/15) and use the same scheduling design: onOneServer and a bounded withoutOverlapping on the commands, a Copenhagen timezone, and a ShouldBeUnique job with UniqueFor shorter than an hour and Tries(1). The difference is how the long job is queued. impl-1 puts the redis-long connection on its own 'long' queue, so only a worker listening there leases the 20-40 minute job, with retry_after 3600 and a 2700s timeout. impl-2's redis-long connection pushes to the same 'default' Redis list as the default redis connection. A normal `queue:work` would pick the job up with retry_after 90 and release it to another worker mid-run, which brings back the double run the task forbids. impl-1 also tests the multi-server and DST cases more convincingly: UTC-based summer/winter checks, three schedule:run calls in one minute, and dispatch after an orphaned lock expires. impl-2 has a uniqueness test that never dispatches twice. impl-2's code is a little more idiomatic: the #[Connection] attribute, and chunkById with the scope re-applied on delete. That does not outweigh the queue-sharing bug.
